problem_register: RC1 WP1.5 (state written by a newer release)

harness.how_it_works: git archive of the revision from local objects into a temp dir; driver runs in 'python -I' subprocess whose import path is only that tree; named modules must import from the tree or the run fails (exit 97); missing revision/path exits 2 with 'revision-unavailable' / 'path-unavailable'; temp tree removed on every exit; working tree, index and HEAD never touched; no network
harness.branch_ci_revision: Branch CI jobs use actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0 (full history, .github/workflows/branch-ci.yml), so e7ec353d6 and d88a1a86f are in the local object database; a shallow clone makes the harness fail with 'revision-unavailable ... shallow clone', never skip
harness.example_other_module: python3 scripts/previous_release_reader.py --revision e7ec353d6 --path services --module services.source_ingestion.requirement_state --driver reader.py -- /path/to/requirement_snapshots.jsonl   (exercised by test_harness_is_reusable_for_another_stateful_service_requirement_state_reader: prints {'sequence': 1, 'binding_count': 2})
harness.fixture_copies: existing checked-in fixture copies were not touched

reproduce_first.method: state written by d88a1a86f (dev before this change) through the harness: default desired state, 32 requirements, collector host and FinMind credential set, all 32 bindings provisioned including collector-tw-trading-holidays, collector-tw-trading-suspension, tw-finmind-monthly-revenue, tw-finmind-quarterly-statements, tw-finmind-valuation; then e7ec353d6 (the 2026-11-17 baseline) reconciled with its own 27-requirement desired state
reproduce_first.detail_text_prefix: provider-owned adapter is not allowlisted: FinMindTaiwanFundamentalsAdapter.records_from_rows; allowed=AdmittedSocialMediaAdapter, ...
reproduce_first.raise_site_at_e7ec353d6: services/source_ingestion/provider_adapters.py:91 validate_provider_adapter_token <- configured.py:401 _validate_fetch_config <- configured.py:260 normalize_fetch_config <- configured.py:243 upsert_config <- runtime.py:1144 _retire_removed_requirement_bindings <- runtime.py:1517 _persona_source_provisioning_payload (translated to HTTP 400 by routers/catalog_controller.py)
reproduce_first.finding: NOT the connector lookup (collector_definition) and NOT persona required_data_sources validation: the baseline's authoritative reconcile treats the five connectors it does not define as 'removed bindings' and tries to DISABLE them by rewriting their stored record, which re-validates a provider adapter token it does not allowlist
reproduce_first.also_observed: with a requirement that names an unknown connector the baseline returns 200 with conflicts=5 (policy_gate_failed); that fails the tick in the worker, not HTTP 400

fix.reconcile: stored connector records, their schedule records and previous snapshot bindings whose provider adapter, connector definition, cadence or dataset this release does not define are skipped; response has skipped[] (kind,id,reason) and skipped_count; nothing is retired, disabled, rewritten or re-validated; requirement naming such a connector is status skipped (not conflict, not unsupported)
fix.bindings: the appended requirement snapshot carries uninterpreted previous bindings forward (32 stays 32 instead of dropping to 27) and each is listed in skipped[] as kind=binding; the snapshot schema is unchanged so older readers still read it
fix.pull_stage: records not defined by this release are reported offered=false so the scheduler skips them instead of failing the pull stage; known connector still runs (test: total_ran 1, total_failed 0)
fix.known_but_invalid: a connector with an allowlisted adapter and an invalid fetch contract still returns HTTP 400 with the existing message (test_known_connector_that_is_malformed_still_fails_closed); requirement/persona validation and unsupported-dataset on a defined connector are unchanged and still fail closed
fix.diagnosability: controller HTTP errors now read 'HTTPError: HTTP Error 400: Bad Request: <detail>' in the tick log line and controller_state last_failure_reason; detail = JSON 'detail' or body text, bounded to 500 characters, bearer token redacted, headers never included; tests: JSON detail, non-JSON body, 5000-char body, structured detail, empty body
fix.readback_health: skipped_count and skipped_ids (first 50) in /api/source-ingest/controller/readback and in /health (via runtime metrics); 0 and [] when nothing is skipped

controller_state_size: one file replaced each tick (asserted: only controller_state.json in the directory, size identical across saves); skipped_ids capped at 50 entries x 128 chars = at most about 6.7 KB added; whole file with 50 ids asserted < 64 KiB

runtime_budget.manifest: docs/operations/storage-manifest.json entry /data/source-ingest/controller_state.json gained changed_fields (cadence, size, cap, cleanup); no other entry edited; scripts/check_storage_manifest.py passed

rollback_proof.method: current code (HEAD) wrote the full state plus a controller_state.json with reconcile.skipped_count=3; e7ec353d6 and d88a1a86f each ran through the harness and read /controller/readback over a copy of the volume
rollback_proof.result: both: HTTP 200, 32 connectors, controller state present, requirement snapshot 32 bindings, no error
rollback_proof.named_difference: neither release knows reconcile.skipped_count / skipped_ids; ControllerState.from_dict ignores unknown keys and the checksum is computed over the payload as written, so reading is safe; their next save rewrites the file without the two fields (safe: the fields are recomputed by the next tick of a release that has them)

hosted_statement: This change cannot repair a release that is already the baseline (e7ec353d6 on 2026-11-17): that code still disables unknown connectors and returns HTTP 400. It protects rollbacks to releases that contain it. After it is served the health payload and controller readback show skipped_count / skipped_ids. The rollback drill from a later release belongs to RC1 WP1.5 of docs/operations/problem-register.md.
